fact: Le Matin reports that Fondation Al Mada with inwi, Managem, Nareva and Injaz Al Maghrib, in collaboration with the Ministry of National Education, is launching a new phase of the Classes Connectees Dir iddik programme equipping 40 more rural primary schools with connected multimedia rooms, with teachers trained in coding, robotics and AI under the ministerial Coding pour Tous programme to run workshops for sixth-year pupils.

The Ministry of Digital Transition (MTNRA) brochure says it launched the JobIntech programme (pilot June 2023, scale-up phase June 2024) and plans to scale up 3-6 month upskilling and reskilling bootcamps and create regional coding schools with public and private partners.
The MTNRA brochure states that 1000 talents had been trained through the JobIntech programme by the end of August 2024.
Le360 reports the creation of Al-Jazari institutes in different regions, aimed at training young people in digital skills.

The minister said two national digital-skills and AI training programmes for ages 8 to 18 were launched: one aimed at nearly 200,000 young people through the football federation, and youth-centre workshops that have reached over 740 children since October 2025.
